transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I’m here because... honestly, it’s just been exhausting. For months now I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern. My sister’s appointments keep getting moved around, the bills show up wrong, and people just conveniently 'forget' to call me back. 

Which is completely unacceptable to me, because I actually supervise an entire team of administrative support workers. I've been running that office for years, ever since I finished my bachelor's, and I tell my girls all the time that details matter. Like Brenda, for instance. She has this terrible habit of just leaving sticky notes on monitors instead of logging things in the system. I had to talk to her about it again right before the holidays. I was actually trying to get out of the office early that day to buy a new collar for my dog—a little red one, because his old one was fraying and I just hate how that looks... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. Even when everyone around me says it’s just mistakes or clerical errors with my sister's things, I know better. I know they’re deliberately keeping information from me. They are trying to push me out of decisions, and I'm not going to just let them pretend it's a coincidence.
Are you absolutely certain that people are deliberately keeping information from you?

Am I certain? Of course I am. You don't just see the exact same pattern for months—the appointments getting moved, the bills showing up wrong, people conveniently forgetting to call back—and just blindly accept that it's a clerical error. I know they are intentionally keeping information from me to push me out of the decisions regarding my sister. It's clear as day. 

Take the bill that came last week, for instance. The mail carrier dropped it off late. He’s a new guy, younger, always wearing his headphones while he walks the route. I just think that’s so unprofessional and frankly dangerous, you know? You can't hear traffic, anyone could sneak up on you. Or a dog could get loose! My neighbor’s golden retriever got out last month and completely trampled my hydrangeas. I was just devastated. I’ve been trying to get the soil pH just right for three years so they’d bloom that really deep, vibrant blue. It takes a lot of aluminum sulfate to get that color, and you have to water it in just perfectly, especially when it hasn't rained... 

But anyway. Yes. Even when everyone else tells me I'm overreacting and that it's just mistakes, I know better. I am absolutely certain they are doing this on purpose to cut me out.
Has anyone been able to convince you that you might be mistaken about people deliberately keeping information from you?

No, absolutely not. No one has convinced me otherwise because I know what I'm seeing. They can tell me it's just mistakes all they want, but like I said, the appointments getting moved, the wrong bills, the unreturned calls—it's all to push me out of decisions about my sister. 

My husband tries to tell me I'm reading too much into it. He says, "Oh, offices are just short-staffed these days." But he doesn't know how an office is supposed to run. He's an engineer. He works with bridges and load-bearing capacities, not people. His firm actually just won a huge contract for that new overpass on Route 9. We went out to dinner to celebrate at this little Italian place downtown. The food was wonderful, but the service was just atrocious. Our waitress took twenty minutes just to bring us water, and when I asked for extra parmesan, she looked at me like I had two heads. I mean, in my office, if one of my girls treated a client like that, there would be a formal write-up. Customer service is a lost art, it really is. People just don't take pride in their work anymore, which is exactly why they think they can get away with this whole charade with my sister's paperwork. 

So, no, no one is going to convince me I'm mistaken. I know they are keeping information from me.
What exactly do you believe they are doing to keep information from you?

Well, it's exactly what I've been saying. They are deliberately moving my sister's appointments around without telling me, sending bills with completely wrong amounts so I can't track the finances, and just conveniently "forgetting" to return my phone calls. It's a coordinated effort to keep me in the dark so I can't make decisions about her care. 

And you know, speaking of phone calls, I just had to upgrade my cell phone last weekend because the battery on my old one wouldn't hold a charge for more than two hours. It was one of those older models with the physical button at the bottom, which I actually prefer. The young man at the store—Tyler, I think his nametag said—tried to talk me into this massive phone that barely fits in my purse. I told him, "Tyler, I don't need to watch movies on my phone, I just need to make calls and check my emails." My purse is already heavy enough as it is. I carry this lovely leather tote I got on sale at Macy's last spring. It has all these wonderful compartments, which is great because I always carry a little emergency sewing kit, some hand sanitizer, and my reading glasses. I actually need to get my prescription checked soon, my left eye has been a little blurry when I read the morning paper. I still get the physical paper delivered, you know, there's just something about holding it in your hands...

But yes, they're moving appointments, messing up the bills, and ignoring my calls. That's how they're keeping the information from me.
Do you ever hear voices or other sounds that other people don’t seem to hear?

Voices? No, certainly not. I don't hear anything that isn't there. Though I will say, the acoustics in my office building are just dreadful, so I hear practically everything else. There's this constant hum from the HVAC system that drives me absolutely up the wall. I put in a maintenance request about it three weeks ago, and the facilities manager—Gary—told me he’d 'look into it.' 

Gary is always saying he'll look into things, but he spends half his day loitering by the vending machines. I actually saw him buying a Diet Coke and a bag of those spicy jalapeño chips yesterday at 10:00 AM. I mean, who eats jalapeño chips at ten in the morning? It is just terrible for your digestion. My husband used to eat spicy foods like that all the time, and he ended up with the most awful acid reflux. We had to completely overhaul our grocery list because of it. I even started buying that special alkaline water, the one in the tall, square bottles? It’s terribly expensive, but you can really taste the difference, especially if you put a little slice of lemon in it. I always keep fresh lemons in the crisper drawer, they just brighten up a glass of water so beautifully... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right, voices. No, I definitely don't hear voices or anything like that. Just the usual noise.
Have you recently had a period where your mood was unusually high or unusually irritable?

Unusually high or irritable? No, my mood has been perfectly normal. Well, normal considering the stress I'm under with everyone trying to push me out of my sister's care. But no, I haven't been running around with boundless energy or snapping at people for no reason. 

Although, speaking of energy, I did try this new matcha green tea last week that my neighbor, Susan, swore by. She told me it gives you this calm, focused energy without the jitters you get from coffee. Susan is always trying these new health trends. Last month it was oil pulling, and before that, it was some sort of celery juice cleanse. She has this gorgeous garden, though—the most beautiful hydrangeas I've ever seen. They're that deep, vibrant blue, which she says is because she alters the pH of the soil with coffee grounds and eggshells. I tried doing that with my rose bushes out front, but it just ended up attracting squirrels. They dug up the entire flowerbed! I had to go to the garden center on Saturday to buy new mulch. The young man who loaded the bags into my trunk was so polite, it was really refreshing. He even put down a piece of cardboard so the dirt wouldn't get on my upholstery. My car is only two years old, it's a Subaru Outback, and I try to keep it immaculate. I just took it through the car wash yesterday, actually, the one on Elm Street that does the undercarriage spray. They always give you those little pine tree air fresheners...

But no, my mood is fine. I'm not unusually high or irritable, just dealing with the situation at hand.
Before all of this with your sister, have you generally tended to distrust other people’s motives?

Distrust people's motives? No, I wouldn't say that at all. I've always been a very trusting person, maybe too trusting sometimes. I mean, I've supervised the administrative staff at my office for fifteen years, and you really have to trust your team to get the job done, don't you? 

Though I will say, you really can't trust the weather forecasters around here. Just last Tuesday, they said it was going to be bright and sunny all day, zero percent chance of rain. So, I decided to wear my new suede loafers—the taupe ones I ordered from Zappos. They were a splurge, but they have this incredible arch support. Anyway, I walked out to get lunch, and it just started pouring. An absolute downpour out of nowhere! My shoes were completely ruined. I tried stuffing them with newspaper to dry them out, which is a trick my grandmother taught me. She used to live in Seattle, so she knew a thing or two about rain. She had this beautiful collection of vintage umbrellas, the kind with the carved wooden handles. I think my cousin Sarah ended up with them after she passed. Sarah always did have a knack for swooping in and claiming the best family heirlooms. She took the good silver, too, the set that came over from Ireland. I only have a few of the teaspoons left, which I keep in a special felt-lined box in my dining room hutch. I really need to polish them before the holidays, they're getting a bit tarnished...

But no, to answer your question, before all this nonsense with my sister's care, I've always been perfectly trusting of people. I don't go around thinking everyone has a hidden agenda, it's just this specific situation where they're clearly trying to keep me out of the loop.
Do you believe anyone is using special methods like cameras, devices, or coded messages to monitor or control what happens with your sister’s care?

Cameras or coded messages? Oh, goodness, no. Nothing like out of a spy movie or anything silly like that. I don't think they're bugging her room or tapping the phones. Though speaking of phones, I had the most frustrating time with my cell phone provider last week. My bill was suddenly twenty dollars higher for no apparent reason, so I called customer service, and I swear I was on hold for forty-five minutes. They play that awful elevator music, you know the kind? It’s just this repetitive synthesizer loop that gets stuck in your head all day. 

When I finally got a real person on the line, she told me I had gone over my data limit, which is just impossible because I barely use my phone outside the house, and I have the Wi-Fi connected. I had to have my nephew come over and show me how to check the data usage in the settings. He's so good with technology, he just graduated with a degree in computer science from State. We took him out to this lovely Italian restaurant to celebrate, the one downtown with the red checkered tablecloths. I had the eggplant parmesan, and it was divine. The portion was so huge I had to take half of it home in a little box. I had it for lunch the next day, and it was almost better leftover, you know how the flavors just meld together in the fridge? I always put a little extra parmesan cheese on top when I reheat it... 

But anyway, no, I don't think anyone is using cameras or secret devices or anything like that. It's just the staff being difficult and trying to keep me away, no gadgets involved.
For how long have you been certain that people are deliberately keeping information from you about your sister’s care?

Well, this whole situation has been going on for about 11 months now. It all started right around the time my sister's health suddenly took a turn for the worse, and I had to step in and start coordinating all her care. 

Which, let me tell you, coordinating care is practically a full-time job in itself. It reminds me of when I was trying to organize the annual summer picnic for my office. I was the one who had to call all the caterers, and you wouldn't believe how hard it is to find a good potato salad. Everyone thinks they make the best potato salad, but most of them just use way too much mayonnaise. I finally found this little deli on 4th Street that puts a hint of Dijon mustard in theirs, which gives it this wonderful tang. I ended up ordering three large tubs of it. We had the picnic at Centennial Park, down by the lake. It's such a lovely spot, except for the geese. You really have to watch where you step because of the geese. One of the junior accountants, bless his heart, wore brand new white sneakers and stepped right in a massive pile of goose droppings. He spent half the afternoon trying to scrape it off with a stick... 

But yes, to answer your question, it's been about 11 months of them deliberately keeping me in the dark since I had to take over her care.
Do you believe the staff are actively plotting together against you?

Plotting together? Well, I don't know if they have secret meetings in a dark room, but they're definitely working together to push me out. I'm here because for months now, I've been seeing the exact same pattern. My sister's appointments get moved without anyone telling me, the bills show up wrong, and people conveniently "forget" to call me back. 

Speaking of forgetting to call back, I tried to get a plumber out to the house last week because the guest bathroom sink was draining so slowly. I called three different places, left voicemails, and not a single one called me back. It’s impossible to find good help these days. I finally had to go under the sink myself and unscrew that little U-shaped pipe—the P-trap, I think it's called? It was absolutely disgusting, just full of hair and soap scum. I had to use an old toothbrush to clean it out. I kept that toothbrush specifically for cleaning grout, you know, because the bristles get perfectly into the little lines between the tiles. I use this homemade mixture of baking soda and vinegar, it bubbles up and works so much better than those harsh chemical sprays. Plus, it doesn't give you a headache. I get terrible tension headaches if I smell bleach for too long...

But anyway, whenever I point out these "mistakes" with my sister's care, everyone just brushes it off. They say, "Oh, it's just an administrative error," or "We're just short-staffed." But I know better. Even when everyone says it's just mistakes, I know they're actively keeping information from me and trying to push me out of making decisions for her. It's too consistent to be an accident.
If the staff showed you clear proof that the appointment changes and billing errors were routine mistakes, would you accept that?

Clear proof? Well, I don't know what they could possibly show me that would change my mind at this point. I mean, they can print out all the spreadsheets and memos they want, but I know what I'm seeing. I've been seeing the exact same pattern for months now—her appointments getting moved around, the bills showing up completely wrong, people conveniently forgetting to call me back. 

It’s like when I was trying to get a refund for that blender I bought at the department store last month. They kept telling me it was a "system error" that my card hadn't been credited. A system error! I had the receipt right there in my purse. It’s one of those big leather tote bags, you know the kind? I bought it at a craft fair last autumn. There was this lovely artisan there who hand-tooled all the leather himself. He had this little stall set up next to a woman selling homemade jams. I bought a jar of her strawberry rhubarb preserve, and oh, it was just heavenly on a piece of toasted sourdough. I started baking my own sourdough during the pandemic, like everyone else did, I suppose. It took me three tries just to get the starter going. You really have to feed it at the exact same time every day, and keep it at the right temperature. I kept mine on top of the refrigerator because it’s just a little bit warmer up there...

But no, to answer your question, I wouldn't accept it. Because even when everyone stands there and says it’s just routine mistakes, I know the truth. They’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of making decisions for her. No piece of paper they show me is going to change what I know is happening.
Do people often tell you that you go off on tangents or have trouble getting to the point when you talk?

No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever come right out and said that to me. I've always thought of myself as a pretty good communicator, actually. You have to be, in my line of work. Managing an office, you're constantly talking to people, making sure everyone is on the same page. 

Like just last Tuesday, we had this massive mix-up with the office supply order. Someone—and I won't name names, but she sits at the front desk and spends half the day looking at shoes online—ordered three boxes of blue pens instead of black. Blue pens! Who uses blue pens for official documents anymore? It looks so unprofessional. I had to call the vendor and sort the whole thing out. The vendor is this lovely man named Gary, he's been our rep for years. He always asks about my cats. I have two, a tabby named Oliver and a calico named Penelope. Penelope is such a picky eater, I have to buy this special grain-free food that costs an absolute fortune, and even then, she'll only eat it if I sprinkle a little bit of chicken broth on top. Not the low-sodium kind either, she won't touch that. It has to be the regular kind. 

But anyway, no, people don't usually say I have trouble getting to the point. I think I'm very clear when I speak.
Outside of your sister’s care, do you currently believe other people are deliberately trying to harm, deceive, or exclude you?

No, no, nothing like that. It's really just the situation at the facility with my sister. Outside of dealing with her appointments and trying to get straight answers from those people, everything else is perfectly fine. I still keep my home in order, I pay my bills on time, and I do my job. 

Actually, speaking of my job, I just organized the most beautiful retirement party for one of our senior accountants, Martha. She's been there for thirty years. We got her this gorgeous sheet cake from that little bakery on 4th Street—the one with the green awning? They do the most incredible buttercream frosting. It's not too sweet, you know? Some places just dump powdered sugar into shortening and call it frosting, but this is real Swiss meringue buttercream. It takes forever to make because you have to heat the egg whites and sugar over a double boiler until it reaches exactly 160 degrees, and then you whip it until the bowl feels cool to the touch before you even think about adding the butter. If the butter is too warm, the whole thing turns into soup, and if it's too cold, it gets all curdled and lumpy. I watched this whole documentary on baking science once when I couldn't sleep. It was fascinating how humidity affects flour absorption...

But anyway, people might think I'm too focused on what's happening with my sister's care, but I'm not falling apart or acting strangely in other parts of my life. I'm just trying to protect her, that's all.
Have you taken any action to protect your sister because you were certain the staff were deliberately keeping information from you?

Well, I've had to be more firm, certainly. I mean, when you know something isn't right, you can't just sit back and let it happen, can you? So yes, I've brought it up at family meetings. But honestly, those have become so tense lately. My brother just sits there looking at his watch, and my sister-in-law gets this pinched look on her face. It's exactly the same look my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Gable, used to get when someone didn't know their multiplication tables. She was a very strict woman, Mrs. Gable. She wore these heavy tweed skirts even in the middle of May, and she always smelled faintly of mothballs and peppermint. I actually started keeping peppermints in my desk at work because of her. The little red and white striped ones, you know? They're quite good for settling the stomach. 

I've needed them at work recently, to be honest. I’ve had a few... uncomfortable conversations there, too. I suppose I’ve been pressing people harder about routine mistakes than I used to. Like with the filing system—if something is misfiled, I need to know *why*, not just that it was an "accident." But I'm still managing all my responsibilities! It’s just... I've noticed it has started to affect how people respond to me. They get quiet when I walk into the breakroom. The breakroom really needs a new microwave, by the way. The one we have now heats everything unevenly. I tried to warm up a bowl of tomato bisque the other day—I made it from scratch over the weekend, roasted the tomatoes with garlic and thyme—and the edges were boiling but the center was ice cold. You really need a microwave with a proper turntable for soup... 

But yes, I've had to take action. I'm just trying to make sure things are done correctly, whether it's for my sister or at the office.
Do you believe your coworkers are deliberately treating you differently because they’re against you?

Against me? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I don't think it's anything malicious. They're just... well, I think they just don't like being held to a high standard, you know? It's certainly not some kind of plot against me. 

Take Sarah, for instance, in payroll. She's not against me at all. We actually used to carpool on Thursdays before she bought that new hybrid car. It's one of those plug-in ones, very quiet. Almost too quiet, really. She nearly backed into a delivery truck last month because the driver couldn't hear her coming in the parking lot. It's a lovely shade of silver, though. I've always liked silver cars, even if they do get terribly dirty in the winter. The salt on the roads around here just coats everything. My father had a silver sedan when I was growing up, and I remember every Sunday morning he would be out in the driveway with a bucket of soapy water and a sponge, washing off the road salt. He used this special wax—Turtle Wax, I think it was called? It came in a little green tub and smelled strongly of coconuts. I always loved that smell. It reminds me of the beach. We used to go to Cape May every summer when I was little, and we'd rent this house with a big wraparound porch... 

But, um... what were we saying? Oh, right, the office. No, my coworkers aren't against me. They just get a bit defensive when I point out their mistakes, that's all.
Despite what other people tell you, are you completely certain that the staff are intentionally keeping information from you?

Yes, I am absolutely certain. I mean, I'm here because for months now I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern. My sister’s appointments get moved without anyone telling me, the bills show up with all these incorrect charges, and people constantly "forget" to call me back. Everyone keeps telling me it’s just administrative mistakes, but I know for a fact they’re keeping information from me. They're trying to push me out of making decisions for her. 

It's just like when you try to cancel a magazine subscription, you know? They make it impossible on purpose. I used to subscribe to this gardening magazine—*Better Blooms*, I think it was called. Beautiful photography, really stunning glossy pages. They had this one issue dedicated entirely to hydrangeas. Did you know that you can change the color of hydrangea blooms by altering the pH of the soil? If you add aluminum sulfate, they turn this gorgeous, vibrant blue, but if the soil is alkaline, they stay pink. I tried it once with a bush in my front yard. I spent weeks measuring out the soil amendments, watering it perfectly, and when it finally bloomed, it was this murky, muddy purple color. Just dreadful. I ended up digging the whole thing up and planting hostas instead. Hostas are so much more reliable, especially in the shade under that big oak tree I have. Though the slugs do love them. You have to put out little shallow dishes of beer to catch the slugs. They just crawl right in... 

But anyway, yes. I know what I'm seeing with my sister's care. They can call it "mistakes" all they want, but I know they are intentionally keeping things from me.
Have you made a formal complaint or accusation against the staff because of what you believe they’re doing?

Well, no, I haven't filed any formal complaints yet. I've thought about it, certainly, but you know how these things go. Once you put something in writing, it becomes this whole bureaucratic nightmare. It's like trying to dispute a charge on your credit card. Have you ever tried to do that? I had this charge show up last month for a streaming service I never signed up for. It was only $8.99, but it's the principle of the thing, isn't it? I spent forty-five minutes on hold listening to this awful, tinny elevator music. It sounded like a pan flute being played underwater. I don't understand why companies can't just play classical music while you wait. A little Mozart or Vivaldi would be so much more soothing. My mother used to play Vivaldi’s *Four Seasons* every Sunday morning while she made breakfast. She made the most incredible Swedish pancakes. They were so thin, almost like crepes, and she’d serve them with lingonberry jam. You can’t really find good lingonberry jam in the regular grocery stores around here. You have to go to that specialty market downtown, the one next to the old movie theater. 

But no, I haven't made a formal accusation against the staff. I've just been keeping a very close eye on things myself.
Do you think there is any chance at all that you might be mistaken about the staff deliberately keeping information from you?

Mistaken? Oh, no. No, absolutely not. I mean, I'm here because for months now I've been seeing the exact same pattern over and over again. My sister's appointments get moved without anyone telling me, the bills show up with all these incorrect charges, people constantly "forget" to call me back. Everyone keeps telling me it's just administrative mistakes, but I know they are keeping information from me. They're trying to push me out of making decisions for her. 

It's just so obvious when you really look at it. It reminds me of this puzzle I used to work on. I love jigsaw puzzles, you know? The really big ones, 1000 pieces or more. I had this one of a Thomas Kinkade painting—a little cottage with glowing windows next to a stream. It took me three weeks to put it together on the dining room table. I had to eat my dinners on a TV tray in the living room the whole time. But anyway, I got to the very end, and there was one piece missing. Just one! Right in the middle of the sky. It drove me absolutely crazy. I searched the floor, under the rug, inside the vacuum cleaner bag—which is a disgusting job, let me tell you. Dust everywhere. I had to wash my hands three times just to get the smell of old dirt off them. I use this wonderful lavender soap from a little boutique in Vermont. We went there on a girls' trip a few years ago in October. The leaves were just spectacular, reds and golds everywhere. We stayed in this bed and breakfast where they made fresh blueberry muffins every morning...

But no, I'm not mistaken. I know exactly what they're doing. They can say it's just mistakes, but I know they're trying to push me out.

Am I certain? Of course I am. You don't just see the exact same pattern for months—the appointments getting moved, the bills showing up wrong, people conveniently forgetting to call back—and just blindly accept that it's a clerical error. None of these specifically address making a formal complaint or accusation.

patient.answer:
Well, no, I haven't filed any formal complaints yet. I've thought about it, certainly, but you know how these things go. Once you put something in writing, it becomes this whole bureaucratic nightmare. It's like trying to dispute a charge on your credit card. Have you ever tried to do that? I had this charge show up last month for a streaming service I never signed up for. It was only $8.99, but it's the principle of the thing, isn't it? I spent forty-five minutes on hold listening to this awful, tinny elevator music. It sounded like a pan flute being played underwater. I don't understand why companies can't just play classical music while you wait. A little Mozart or Vivaldi would be so much more soothing. My mother used to play Vivaldi’s *Four Seasons* every Sunday morning while she made breakfast. She made the most incredible Swedish pancakes. They were so thin, almost like crepes, and she’d serve them with lingonberry jam. You can’t really find good lingonberry jam in the regular grocery stores around here. You have to go to that specialty market downtown, the one next to the old movie theater. 

But no, I haven't made a formal accusation against the staff. I've just been keeping a very close eye on things myself.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the fixed persecutory belief is accompanied by poor insight in a way more consistent with delusional disorder than a paranoid or anankastic personality style.
doctor.question: Do you think there is any chance at all that you might be mistaken about the staff deliberately keeping information from you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been seeing the same pattern—my sister’s appointments get moved, bills show up wrong, people 'forget' to call me back—and even when everyone says it’s just mistakes, I know they’re keeping information from me and trying to push me out of decisions.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if there is any chance the patient might be mistaken about their belief, which directly probes the 'fixed' nature of the belief, a core component of the 'Delusions' symptom profile.

patient.answer:
Mistaken? Oh, no. No, absolutely not. I mean, I'm here because for months now I've been seeing the exact same pattern over and over again. My sister's appointments get moved without anyone telling me, the bills show up with all these incorrect charges, people constantly "forget" to call me back. Everyone keeps telling me it's just administrative mistakes, but I know they are keeping information from me. They're trying to push me out of making decisions for her. 

It's just so obvious when you really look at it. It reminds me of this puzzle I used to work on. I love jigsaw puzzles, you know? The really big ones, 1000 pieces or more. I had this one of a Thomas Kinkade painting—a little cottage with glowing windows next to a stream. It took me three weeks to put it together on the dining room table. I had to eat my dinners on a TV tray in the living room the whole time. But anyway, I got to the very end, and there was one piece missing. Just one! Right in the middle of the sky. It drove me absolutely crazy. I searched the floor, under the rug, inside the vacuum cleaner bag—which is a disgusting job, let me tell you. Dust everywhere. I had to wash my hands three times just to get the smell of old dirt off them. I use this wonderful lavender soap from a little boutique in Vermont. We went there on a girls' trip a few years ago in October. The leaves were just spectacular, reds and golds everywhere. We stayed in this bed and breakfast where they made fresh blueberry muffins every morning...

But no, I'm not mistaken. I know exactly what they're doing. They can say it's just mistakes, but I know they're trying to push me out.

opening_question.intent: Elicit the patient's main presenting problem
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a fixed, non-bizarre persecutory belief lasting about 11 months that staff are deliberately withholding information and excluding her from decisions about her sister’s care. She is completely convinced, cannot be persuaded otherwise, and the belief is circumscribed rather than part of a broader lifelong suspicious personality pattern. She denies hallucinations, bizarre surveillance/control beliefs, and manic symptoms, supporting a delusional disorder rather than paranoid personality disorder or anankastic personality disorder.
